newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan April overseas ship orders up 40 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Japan April overseas ship orders up 40 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Ship export contracts concluded by Japanese shipyards in April totalled 19 vessels, or 746,850 gross registered tons (grt), an increase of 39.4 percent from a year ago, an industry body said on Tuesday.
The sharp rise can be partly attributed to the fact that a Japanese firm won a contract for a very large crude carrier (VLCC) in April, the Japan Ship Exporters' Association said.
Orders for April comprised two freighters, 10 bulk carriers, three dirty tankers including one VLCC, two clean tankers and two liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) ships.

From January through April, Japan received ship orders for 102 vessels, or 3.88 million grt, while South Korea, another major ship builder, won orders for 42 ships totalling 2.87 million grt during the same period, a spokesman for the association said.
